text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000034 bills 99215 at about four times the complexity-adjusted expectation, mostly on patients with few or no chronic conditions, but records are too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward concern. The excess 99215 volume falls mainly on 0–1 condition patients, where this provider's 99215 share runs well above the all-provider share. Sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry simple diagnoses such as Z09 follow-ups, R21 rash and M54.50 back pain (e.g., C0020956, C0020890, C0020893). Few complex patients like C0021273 appear among them. The documentation does not settle the question: only one 99215 chart was returned, and it supported the billed level (C0020986), while the single 99214 mismatch (C0021418) is within normal documentation noise. The 3 notes claiming moderate-plus data review with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence of possible note inflation, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, particularly the Z09 and R21 visits, to see whether documented MDM and time support level 5."}
